channel.title: The Wilson Times - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Wilson Times (wilsontimes.com)

item.title: Pittman claims too much credit for school funding
item.description: Wilson County school board member John Kyle says Rep. Dante Pittman is overstating his role in a $42 million school grant, arguing that credit belongs to a broader team.

item.title: Sorority celebrates 85 years of service and sisterhood
item.description: Alpha Kappa Alpha’s Gamma Beta Omega Chapter marks 85 years in Wilson, honoring its legacy of service and sisterhood with civic leaders, community awards and a message on leadership and impact.

item.title: Stantonsburg’s future is looking brighter
item.description: New Stantonsburg council members bring optimism with plans to revive the police department and fix finances, even as a controversial closed-session decision exposes gaps in leadership.

item.title: The vanishing penny and why exact change still matters
item.description: As Wilson shops quietly drop pennies and round bills, cash customers are losing money cent by cent — even though the penny is still legal tender and exact change is required.

item.title: Wreaths to be placed on veterans’ graves Saturday
item.description: Rest Haven Cemetery will honor veterans Saturday as volunteers place 216 donated wreaths on graves, with a jet flyover and calls for expanded support to reach more veterans in future years.

item.title: ‘The people voted for change’: New council takes office
item.description: Wilson's new City Council signaled a voter-backed shift in direction, including a surprise 4–3 vote shakeup in the mayor pro tem role.

item.title: NCHSAA CHAMPIONSHIP NOTEBOOK: Tigers senior trio rewarded with state championshp
item.description: In just its fourth season, Wilson Prep captured its first NCHSAA 1-A football title with a 9-8 win over Robbinsville, as seniors Travon Usher, Ethan Nelson and Manny Dickens delivered clutch plays in the frantic final minutes.

item.title: Dickens’ expectations for Tigers based on faith
item.description: How coach Phillip Dickens turned Wilson Prep’s fledgling football program into a 1-A title contender, using faith, adversity and a brutal schedule to forge a championship mindset.

item.title: Organizers receive donations
item.description: Local groups have added funds to help with their community projects thanks to American Legion Post 13.

item.title: 2 more candidates file for Wilson County sheriff
item.description: A Nash County deputy and Enfield police officer are joining the race to replace Wilson County Sheriff Calvin Woodard, who is not running.
